name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Tectonic Charge TC-5 'Fault Line'
description: A specialized demolition charge designed to be buried or anchored to structural foundations, detonating with a shaped downward blast that fractures bedrock and disrupts structural footing. The TC-5 uses Zheng-Dao's resonant detonation technology — the charge fires in a precisely timed sequence of micro-detonations that amplify through the ground substrate like an artificial earthquake, causing foundation failure across a much larger area than the charge's raw explosive yield would suggest. Originally developed for mining and geological survey, the TC-5 has become the preferred tool for infrastructure sabotage — a single charge can collapse a building by undermining its foundations without any visible surface damage.
legality: Licensed — demolition and mining; Prohibited — all other use
specifications:
explosive yield: Equivalent to 5 kg TNT, amplified by resonant detonation
effect radius: 20-meter foundation disruption zone
placement: Buried 1-2 meters or anchored to foundation
detonation sequence: 12-stage resonant micro-detonation over 0.8 seconds
timer options: 30 seconds to 72 hours, or remote trigger
weight: 3.2 kg per charge
form factor: Flat disc, 25 cm diameter
story_hooks: Three buildings have collapsed in a straight line across Tier 2 over three weeks — geological analysis shows resonant detonation signatures beneath each, suggesting a deliberate campaign of infrastructure destruction.

A TC-5 charge has been found planted beneath a major transit hub but not detonated — the timer was set but the trigger signal never came, suggesting the planter was interrupted or the charge is a warning.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Resonance Hammer RH-3 'Earthquake'

physical_description.visual_profile: A flat, hockey-puck-shaped demolition charge with a deliberately industrial aesthetic—no curves, no ergonomics. It's a tool designed to be buried and forgotten. The top surface features a recessed circular panel with precision-machined grooves radiating outward from a central detonation node, suggesting the internal resonance chambers within.
physical_description.dimensions: 25 cm diameter × 8 cm height. Compact enough to palm, heavy enough to demand respect.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and dense despite modest size—3.2 kg creates genuine heft in the hand, pulling downward. The weight distribution is perfectly centered, making it feel like holding a shot put made of lead and malice.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite body with internal steel resonance chambers visible through translucent sections. The exterior casing is injection-molded for precision, with microscopic stress-relief patterns etched into the surface.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with brushed steel accent panels. The top surface has a subtle anodized bronze tone highlighting the resonance groove array. Light surface oxidation and micro-scratches suggest heavy field use despite the 'new' appearance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with bronze and steel accents. No branding colors—purely utilitarian. A single red dot marks the detonation point on top.
physical_description.grip_texture: The beveled edge is textured with a crosshatch pattern for secure handling while wearing demolition gloves. The surface has subtle grip indentations molded into the bottom, preventing rotation when placed.
distinctive_features: Radial resonance chamber grooves etched across the top surface in a precise geometric pattern
Central detonation node marked by a recessed steel circle with a single red indicator dot
Translucent polymer sections on the side revealing internal steel reinforcement framework
Timer/trigger interface port hidden beneath a spring-loaded panel on the base (keeps debris out during burial)
Safety interlocks visible as raised ridges forming a circuit pattern around the circumference
Zheng-Dao serial number laser-etched on the bottom in micro-text
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: The Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries logo—a stylized tectonic plate symbol—is etched in bronze on one side panel. The model designation 'TC-5' and 'FAULT LINE' are stamped beneath in small raised characters. A licensing barcode occupies the bottom center.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually pristine before deployment, but field specimens show dust residue, minor dents from transport, and scratches from rough handling. Never visibly damaged—failure is not an option. Post-deployment examples are simply gone.
